NOTES:
Setting is late autumn 1348 during the Black Death in the isolated village of Ravenhollow.
Villagers believe the pestilence is God's ultimate punishment.
The churchyard graves are shallow and waterlogged.
The entity that awakens the buried dead is ancient and unseen; the story deliberately conceals its nature, origins, and physical form.

In the autumn of 1348, the villagers of Ravenhollow believed the pestilence was the worst thing God could send them. They were wrong.
A solitary traveler arrived at the parish gates as dusk settled over the frozen mud. His woolen cloak was drenched in rain, and his boots were encrusted with grey clay.
Father Thomas opened the sanctuary doors, raising a bronze lantern into the damp mist. Behind him, frightened villagers huddled along the stone nave, clutching bone rosaries in trembling hands.
The traveler collapsed onto the cold flags before the altar. He whispered that the freshly dug graves behind the church were moving, as if hands beneath the earth were clawing upward through the frozen soil.
Outside, beneath the dripping yew trees, the damp turf of the mass trench began to heave. Pine coffin lids splintered under rhythmic scratching, as if something from within were trying to pry them open.
A milk-white boy with bare blue-tinged feet stood motionless at the edge of the cemetery path, his hollow eyes fixed on the chapel bell tower.
The church bell began to toll with no human hand upon the rope. Inside the nave, Father Thomas knelt and prayed, his voice breaking as the heavy oak doors rattled against their iron bolts.
In the moonlit churchyard, the earth split open across dozens of graves. Shadows stirred in the mist as the dead stood upright among the leaning headstones, summoned by a silent call from the dark beneath the earth.
